newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Quiet Russian shares flat, seen unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Russian shares flat, seen unchanged.

text.p: Range-bound leading Russian shares closed flat on Thursday flat on relatively light volumes, and traders said they expected sluggish trade to last into Friday.

The Russian Trading System (RTS) 24-share index closed down 0.4 percent at 275.49 on $18.7 million volume for the entire market, less than a third of the volume seen on Friday when the RTS hit a record 293.33.
Rostelekom edged up to $3.50 from $3.49 at Wednesday's close and Mosenergo ticked up to $1.50 from $1.49.
Dealers said they expected more trading within a percentage point or two of current levels in the near future while the market waits for a new stream of Western orders.
"Most deals were happening at bid or offer, depending on the interest of the initiator," said Renaissance Capital trader Oleg Tatkov, pointing to the lack of liquidity in the market.
Some interest for second-tier shares was seen and Chelyabenergo rose to $0.355 from $0.285 after news of improved nine-months earnings were released.
"Second-tier utilities and telecoms should do better from blue chips slowing down," Tatkov said.

Purneftegaz shares fell to $3.51 from $3.70 after a Russian court ruled that Rosneft would keep the oil production unit sought by SIDANKO, and dealers said fears that the battle would continue had hit the share price.
Dealers said the market had also been slow as exhausted operators recovered from three weeks of a bull run.
"It is not just a question of psychological exhaustion -- it is physical exhaustion as well," said Trinfiko salesman Alexander Gritskevich.
